title: Is this coefficient big enough?
hints: The most one digit can add is its coefficient times its largest value, not the coefficient alone.
Look at the comparison. When c equals the most the digits can add, two offsets are the same, so the answer must be no.
Add up d * m over the digits, then return c > most.
prompt: fits(c, digits) answers one question of the rule: is the coefficient c greater than the most the smaller digits can add up to? Each digit is a pair (coefficient, largest value). The function is nearly written, and it is wrong in two places. It adds up the coefficients and forgets the largest values. And it says yes when c only equals the total. Fix both.

answer.explain: A digit with coefficient d and largest value m adds at most d * m, so the most the digits add together is the sum of those products. The coefficient c has to be strictly greater. With 3 and a digit that reaches 3, the offsets 3*1 + 0 and 3*0 + 3 are both 3, which is a collision.
